name: eTracker Analytics

suggests.drupal/cookies: Cookie consent management; enable the bundled cookies_etracker submodule to gate the tracker on consent.
suggests.drupal/csp: Content-Security-Policy module; etracker adds its tracking domain to script-src via an event subscriber.

project_description: The eTracker Analytics module integrates the etracker web-analytics service into Drupal by attaching etracker's client-side tracking snippet to configured pages. hook_library_info_build() defines an external script library pointing at https://code.etracker.com/code/e.js and emits the configured account key as the tracking tag's data-secure-code attribute, together with data-block-cookies and data-respect-dnt flags. hook_page_attachments() then, when the current path/role/user is in scope, attaches that library plus an inline <head> script that passes the current page title (and an optional breadcrumb-derived et_areas hierarchy) to etracker, all rawurlencoded. An admin settings form (route etracker.admin_settings_form at /admin/config/system/etracker, permission 'administer etracker') writes the etracker.settings config object: account key, script position (header/footer), page/role visibility rules, per-user opt-in/out, breadcrumb-as-area mode, Do-Not-Track and cookie-blocking privacy flags, and client-side event tracking for mailto/outbound/download links and Drupal system messages. A per-user opt-in/out checkbox is added to the user form for holders of the 'opt-in or out of etracker tracking' permission. When the csp module is present, CspSubscriber adds the etracker domain to the CSP script-src directive. The optional cookies_etracker submodule integrates with the COOKiES consent module to gate the tracker on visitor consent. An etracker account (a paid service) is required.
